claims.text: In docs/team/sprint-example.md, 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy' has estimate 2 and final status 'Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau'; the file does not say why it took longer.
The sprint review section says the 'Ngừng gửi thông báo' item was not shown because it was not finished; unfinished work is not counted even with almost all the code written.

The retrospective lists: did well (acceptance criteria before code), needs fixing (work depending on a single person), action (items larger than 3 points must have two people read the code); no line mentions estimates.

An estimate is a guess about size made before the work starts; an item not finishing does not make its estimate wrong; only after the work can the team compare the guess with reality, at the retrospective.
Treating estimates as commitments pushes people to protect themselves: bigger numbers next time, or calling unfinished work done; either way the numbers stop describing the work.

self_check.notes: Quotes sprint-example.md@stage-0 lines 31-33 and 37-39 (no ## headings). Outline item 2 says 'lowball'; lesson says bigger numbers to stay consistent with approved why-estimate (DECISIONS.md §3). No velocity, no buffer.
